content.text:
I read the release in full and checked every figure in the brief against it. Here is the verification.

**Part 1 summary:** All ten key facts are stated correctly. The brief uses more precise figures than the fact list in several places ($11.633B vs $11.6B, $4.756B vs $4.8B, $6.042B vs $6.0B, $3.853B vs $3.9B), which round correctly to the precision shown. Basis labels (GAAP vs non-GAAP), the quarter versus nine-month distinction, and constant-dollar versus nominal are all handled correctly — notably the brief keeps the $563M severance and $237M MDL provision on the GAAP side rather than presenting non-GAAP results as reported, and it correctly reports the Q3 payments volume (+10%) separately from the March-quarter volume (+9%) that drives service revenue.

**Part 2 summary:** I found no unsupported claims. Two items worth flagging for context rather than as errors: (1) the brief's "largest revenue category" and "slowest of Visa's revenue categories" framings from the fact list are not explicitly asserted in the brief, but it lists every revenue line with figures, so nothing is contradicted; (2) the Outlook section's assertion that the release gives no guidance is an absence claim — it is accurate, as the release contains only the forward-looking-statements disclaimer and risk factor list, with no forward targets.

facts.evidence: Net revenue was $11.633 billion, an increase of 14% (13% on a constant-dollar basis), which the release attributes to growth in payments volume, cross-border volume and processed transactions.
GAAP net income was $5.628 billion (+7%) and GAAP diluted class A EPS was $2.97 (+10%; approximately 9% on a constant-dollar basis).
Non-GAAP net income was $6.296 billion (+8%) and non-GAAP diluted EPS was $3.32 (+11%; approximately 11% constant-dollar).
Revenue lines: service revenue $4.922 billion (+14%), data processing $6.042 billion (+17%), international transaction $3.853 billion (+6%), other revenue $1.496 billion (+45%).
GAAP operating expenses were $4.756 billion, up 19%, primarily driven by higher personnel expense; non-GAAP operating expenses rose 17%, primarily on marketing and personnel.
Constant-dollar drivers for the quarter: payments volume +10%, cross-border volume excluding intra-Europe +12%, total cross-border volume +13%, processed transactions +10% (71.7 billion).
Share repurchases and dividends totaled $6.2 billion in the quarter
Cash, cash equivalents and investment securities were $13.9 billion at June 30, 2026.
GAAP results include special items of $563 million in severance costs, a $237 million MDL litigation provision and an $18 million deferred tax benefit
international transaction $3.853 billion (+6%) ... International transaction revenue grew 6% while total cross-border volume rose 13% constant-dollar (15% nominal)

claims.claim: Visa's fiscal Q3 2026 net revenue was $11.6 billion, up 14%, or 13% on a constant-dollar basis.
Fiscal Q3 2026 GAAP EPS was $2.97 and non-GAAP EPS was $3.32.
All four key business drivers grew at double-digit rates.
Net revenue was $11.633 billion.
The release attributes net revenue growth to year-over-year growth in payments volume, cross-border volume and processed transactions.
GAAP net income was $5.628 billion, an increase of 7%.
GAAP diluted class A EPS was $2.97, up 10%, and approximately 9% on a constant-dollar basis.
Non-GAAP net income was $6.296 billion, an increase of 8%.
Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $3.32, up 11%, and approximately 11% on a constant-dollar basis.
GAAP results include a special item of $563 million in severance costs.
GAAP results include a $237 million litigation provision associated with the interchange MDL case.
GAAP results include an $18 million deferred tax benefit.
Current-year results include $9 million of net equity investment losses.
Current-year results include $78 million of acquired-intangible amortization and acquisition-related costs.
Prior-year results included a $615 million litigation provision.
Prior-year results included $35 million of net equity investment losses.
Prior-year results included $73 million of amortization of acquired intangibles and acquisition-related costs.
GAAP operating expenses were $4.756 billion, up 19%, primarily driven by higher personnel expense.
Non-GAAP operating expenses rose 17%, primarily driven by marketing and personnel expenses.
The GAAP effective income tax rate was 17.6% for the quarter.
The non-GAAP effective income tax rate was 18.4% for the quarter.
On a constant-dollar basis for the quarter, payments volume rose 10%, cross-border volume excluding intra-Europe rose 12%, total cross-border volume rose 13% and processed transactions rose 10%.
Processed transactions were 71.7 billion in the quarter.
On a nominal basis, payments volume rose 11%, cross-border volume excluding intra-Europe rose 14%, total cross-border volume rose 15% and processed transactions rose 10%.
Service revenue was $4.922 billion, up 14%.
Data processing revenue was $6.042 billion, up 17%.
International transaction revenue was $3.853 billion, up 6%.
Other revenue was $1.496 billion, up 45%.
Client incentives were $4.680 billion, up 18%.
Service revenue is recognized based on the prior quarter's payments volume.
Payments volume for the three months ended March 31, 2026 rose 9% on a constant-dollar basis.
The release provides no financial guidance or outlook for any future period, containing only a forward-looking-statements disclaimer and risk factors, with no revenue, EPS or volume targets.
Share repurchases and dividends totaled $6.2 billion in the fiscal third quarter.
Visa repurchased approximately 14.5 million class A shares at an average cost of $330.71 per share for $4.9 billion during the quarter.
Visa had $28.4 billion of remaining authorized repurchase funds as of June 30, 2026.
A quarterly cash dividend of $0.670 per class A share was declared on July 28, 2026.
Cash, cash equivalents and investment securities were $13.9 billion at June 30, 2026.
Accrued litigation was $1.274 billion at June 30, 2026 versus $3.033 billion at September 30, 2025.
Restricted cash equivalents in the U.S. litigation escrow were $888 million versus $2.990 billion at September 30, 2025.
On June 25, 2026, Visa deposited $250 million into the litigation escrow account, reducing as-converted class B-1, B-2 and B-3 share counts at a volume-weighted average price of $333.42.
The class B-1/class B-2 exchange offer settled on May 12, 2026.
International transaction revenue grew 6% while total cross-border volume rose 13% on a constant-dollar basis and 15% nominal.
Interest expense was $194 million in the quarter versus $39 million in the prior-year quarter.
The balance sheet shows long-term debt of $20.862 billion versus $19.602 billion at September 30, 2025.
Other revenue rose 45% and client incentives rose 18%, against 14% net revenue growth.
